opening.text: Before a long trip, most of us look at a map. We want to know where we are, where we are going, and how to get there. Without one, we wander.
Life can feel the same way. We ask big questions. Where did I come from? Why am I here? Where am I going? God has given us a map. It is called the plan of happiness. I would like to talk about it.

mainMessage.text: Before we were born, we lived with our Heavenly Father. He made a plan so we could grow and become like Him. The Savior was chosen to make that plan possible. We came to earth to be tested and to learn. We are free to choose. And if we follow the Savior, we can return to God and live with our families forever. Every part of the plan was built on love.

blocks.text: We lived with God before we were born.
The plan begins before the earth. Abraham was shown spirits who lived before the world was. And when God laid the foundations of the earth, the sons of God shouted for joy. We were part of that.

Now the Lord had shown unto me, Abraham, the intelligences that were organized before the world was; and among all these there were many of the noble and great ones; And God saw these souls that they were good, and he stood in the midst of them, and he said: These I will make my rulers; for he stood among those that were spirits, and he saw that they were good; and he said unto me: Abraham, thou art one of them; thou wast chosen before thou wast born.
Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding. . . . When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
President Spencer W. Kimball wrote this in his book Faith Precedes the Miracle, page 97. It is a book, not a conference talk.

If we looked at mortality as the whole of existence, then pain, sorrow, failure, and short life would be calamity. But if we look upon life as an eternal thing stretching far into the premortal past and on into the eternal post-death future, then all happenings may be put in proper perspective.
Life is bigger than the part we can see.
God made a plan.

Heavenly Father did not leave us to guess. He called a council and laid out a plan. An earth would be made. We would be proved there. Those who do well would receive more. Alma called this the great plan of happiness.

And there stood one among them that was like unto God, and he said unto those who were with him: We will go down, for there is space there, and we will take of these materials, and we will make an earth whereon these may dwell; And we will prove them herewith, to see if they will do all things whatsoever the Lord their God shall command them; And they who keep their first estate shall be added upon; and they who keep not their first estate shall not have glory in the same kingdom with those who keep their first estate; and they who keep their second estate shall have glory added upon their heads for ever and ever.
Now behold, it was not expedient that man should be reclaimed from this temporal death, for that would destroy the great plan of happiness.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Creation” from the April 2000 general conference.

The plan required the Creation, and that in turn required both the Fall and the Atonement. These are the three fundamental components of the plan. The creation of a paradisiacal planet came from God. Mortality and death came into the world through the Fall of Adam. Immortality and the possibility of eternal life were provided by the Atonement of Jesus Christ. The Creation, the Fall, and the Atonement were planned long before the actual work of the Creation began.
Three parts, one plan. Each one matters.
The Savior was chosen to make it work.

A plan needs someone to carry it out. Two stepped forward. One said, “Give me thine honor.” The Beloved Son said, “Thy will be done, and the glory be thine forever.” Without the Savior, Alma said, all mankind must perish.

And I, the Lord God, spake unto Moses, saying: That Satan, whom thou hast commanded in the name of mine Only Begotten, is the same which was from the beginning, and he came before me, saying—Behold, here am I, send me, I will be thy son, and I will redeem all mankind, that one soul shall not be lost, and surely I will do it; wherefore give me thine honor. But, behold, my Beloved Son, which was my Beloved and Chosen from the beginning, said unto me—Father, thy will be done, and the glory be thine forever.

For it is expedient that an atonement should be made; for according to the great plan of the Eternal God there must be an atonement made, or else all mankind must unavoidably perish; yea, all are hardened; yea, all are fallen and are lost, and must perish except it be through the atonement which it is expedient should be made.

Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this about the Atonement of Jesus Christ in his article “Missionary Work and the Atonement” in the March 2001 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.
the central fact, the crucial foundation, and the chief doctrine of the great and eternal plan of salvation.
He is the center. Without Him, there is no plan.
Earth life is for growing.

We did not come here to coast. Adam fell that men might be, and men are that they might have joy. Alma taught that this life is the time to prepare to meet God. Growth takes time, and effort, and sometimes struggle.
Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy.
For behold, this life is the time for men to prepare to meet God; yea, behold the day of this life is the day for men to perform their labors.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Born Again” from the April 2008 general conference.

You may ask, Why doesn’t this mighty change happen more quickly with me? . . . For most of us, the changes are more gradual and occur over time. Being born again . . . is more a process than an event. And engaging in that process is the central purpose of mortality.
Joy and growth go together.
We are free to choose.

A plan with no choices would be a plan with no growth. Lehi taught his son that we are free to choose liberty and eternal life, or captivity and death. And Joshua said it plainly: choose you this day whom ye will serve.

Wherefore, men are free according to the flesh; and all things are given them which are expedient unto man. And they are free to choose liberty and eternal life, through the great Mediator of all men, or to choose captivity and death, according to the captivity and power of the devil; for he seeketh that all men might be miserable like unto himself.

And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.
Elder Neal A. Maxwell of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this in his book One More Strain of Praise, page 80. It is a book, not a conference talk.

Without the existence of choices, without our freedom to choose and without opposition, there would be no real existence. . . . It is a fact that we can neither grow spiritually nor thereby be truly happy unless and until we make wise use of our moral agency.
Our choices are how we grow.
The plan leads home.

At death, our spirits go home to God who gave them life. For the righteous, there is paradise, a state of rest. And Jesus promised there is a place prepared for us in His Father’s house. The plan ends where it began, with God.

Now, concerning the state of the soul between death and the resurrection—Behold, it has been made known unto me by an angel, that the spirits of all men, as soon as they are departed from this mortal body, yea, the spirits of all men, whether they be good or evil, are taken home to that God who gave them life.

In my Father’s house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also.

“The Family: A Proclamation to the World” was read by President Gordon B. Hinckley at the general Relief Society meeting in September 1995. It was signed by the First Presidency and the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles. It is printed in the Ensign, Nov. 1995, page 102.

\[Heavenly Father’s\] divine plan of happiness enables family relationships to be perpetuated beyond the grave. Sacred ordinances and covenants available in holy temples make it possible for individuals to return to the presence of God and for families to be united eternally.
Home is where God is, and where our families can be.

story.title: Adam and Eve rejoice in the plan

blocks.text: Adam and Eve left the garden. Their life became harder. But they understood why. They saw the plan, and they were glad.

And in that day Adam blessed God and was filled, and began to prophesy concerning all the families of the earth, saying: Blessed be the name of God, for because of my transgression my eyes are opened, and in this life I shall have joy, and again in the flesh I shall see God. And Eve, his wife, heard all these things and was glad, saying: Were it not for our transgression we never should have had seed, and never should have known good and evil, and the joy of our redemption, and the eternal life which God giveth unto all the obedient. And Adam and Eve blessed the name of God, and they made all things known unto their sons and their daughters.
They did not say, “Look what we lost.” They said, “Look what we gained.” When we see the plan, we can face hard days with hope. And like them, we can share what we know with our children.

application.text: First, write down three questions the plan answers: Where did I come from? Why am I here? Where am I going? Answer each in one sentence. Second, make one choice this week with the plan in mind. Choose the thing that moves you toward God. Third, share the plan with someone who is struggling. Keep it simple and kind.

story.title: Joseph forgives his brothers

blocks.text: Joseph’s brothers had sold him into slavery. Years later, he was a ruler in Egypt, and they came to him afraid. He could have punished them. He did not.

And Joseph said unto them, Fear not: for am I in the place of God? But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive. Now therefore fear ye not: I will nourish you, and your little ones. And he comforted them, and spake kindly unto them.
Joseph could see the bigger plan. What was meant for harm, God used for good. When we trust that there is a plan behind our trials, we can forgive and keep going.

application.text: First, think of a hard time in your life. Ask where God may have used it for good. Second, take one step this week that fits the plan: pray, read scripture, or serve someone. Third, talk with your family about the plan, and ask what questions they have.

story.title: Lehi’s dream of the tree of life

blocks.text: Lehi dreamed of a tree. It stood for the love of God. He tasted its fruit, and the first thing he wanted was to share it.

And it came to pass that I beheld a tree, whose fruit was desirable to make one happy. And it came to pass that I did go forth and partake of the fruit thereof; and I beheld that it was most sweet, above all that I ever before tasted. Yea, and I beheld that the fruit thereof was white, to exceed all the whiteness that I had ever seen. And as I partook of the fruit thereof it filled my soul with exceedingly great joy; wherefore, I began to be desirous that my family should partake of it also; for I knew that it was desirable above all other fruit.
The plan is meant to make us happy. And when we find that happiness, we want our families to have it too. That is the plan at its best.

application.text: First, ask yourself what lesson you think God is teaching you right now. Write it down. Second, do one thing this week that shows you trust His plan: pray, read, serve, or forgive. Third, think of one family member you want to share the plan with. Ask Heavenly Father how.

The trail was mapped by God.
The Lord said we would go down to an earth and be proved there. Those who keep their estates would receive more. Alma called this the great plan of happiness.

And there stood one among them that was like unto God, and he said unto those who were with him: We will go down, for there is space there, and we will take of these materials, and we will make an earth whereon these may dwell; And we will prove them herewith, to see if they will do all things whatsoever the Lord their God shall command them; And they who keep their first estate shall be added upon; and they who keep not their first estate shall not have glory in the same kingdom with those who keep their first estate; and they who keep their second estate shall have glory added upon their heads for ever and ever.
Now behold, it was not expedient that man should be reclaimed from this temporal death, for that would destroy the great plan of happiness.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Creation” from the April 2000 general conference.

The plan required the Creation, and that in turn required both the Fall and the Atonement. These are the three fundamental components of the plan. The creation of a paradisiacal planet came from God. Mortality and death came into the world through the Fall of Adam. Immortality and the possibility of eternal life were provided by the Atonement of Jesus Christ. The Creation, the Fall, and the Atonement were planned long before the actual work of the Creation began.
The map has three markers: Creation, Fall, Atonement.
The Guide is the Savior.
No one hikes a hard trail alone. We have a Guide who chose to help. He said, “Father, thy will be done.” Alma taught that without an atonement, all would be lost.

And I, the Lord God, spake unto Moses, saying: That Satan, whom thou hast commanded in the name of mine Only Begotten, is the same which was from the beginning, and he came before me, saying—Behold, here am I, send me, I will be thy son, and I will redeem all mankind, that one soul shall not be lost, and surely I will do it; wherefore give me thine honor. But, behold, my Beloved Son, which was my Beloved and Chosen from the beginning, said unto me—Father, thy will be done, and the glory be thine forever.

For it is expedient that an atonement should be made; for according to the great plan of the Eternal God there must be an atonement made, or else all mankind must unavoidably perish; yea, all are hardened; yea, all are fallen and are lost, and must perish except it be through the atonement which it is expedient should be made.

Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this about the Atonement of Jesus Christ in his article “Missionary Work and the Atonement” in the March 2001 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.
the central fact, the crucial foundation, and the chief doctrine of the great and eternal plan of salvation.
With Him as guide, we can finish.
The trail is for climbing.
A flat trail would be easy, but no one would grow. Adam fell that men might be, and men are that they might have joy. This life is the time to prepare to meet God.
Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy.
For behold, this life is the time for men to prepare to meet God; yea, behold the day of this life is the day for men to perform their labors.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Born Again” from the April 2008 general conference.

You may ask, Why doesn’t this mighty change happen more quickly with me? . . . For most of us, the changes are more gradual and occur over time. Being born again . . . is more a process than an event. And engaging in that process is the central purpose of mortality.
Keep walking. Step by step is how it is done.
We choose each turn.
The trail forks many times. No one can choose for us. Lehi taught that we are free to choose liberty and eternal life or captivity and death. Joshua made his choice, and he called others to choose.

Wherefore, men are free according to the flesh; and all things are given them which are expedient unto man. And they are free to choose liberty and eternal life, through the great Mediator of all men, or to choose captivity and death, according to the captivity and power of the devil; for he seeketh that all men might be miserable like unto himself.

And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.
Elder Neal A. Maxwell of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this in his book One More Strain of Praise, page 80. It is a book, not a conference talk.

Without the existence of choices, without our freedom to choose and without opposition, there would be no real existence. . . . It is a fact that we can neither grow spiritually nor thereby be truly happy unless and until we make wise use of our moral agency.
Every turn is a choice. Choose the path that leads home.
The trail ends at home.
At the end, there is a home. Our spirits return to God who gave them life, and Jesus is preparing a place for us. Families can be there together.

Now, concerning the state of the soul between death and the resurrection—Behold, it has been made known unto me by an angel, that the spirits of all men, as soon as they are departed from this mortal body, yea, the spirits of all men, whether they be good or evil, are taken home to that God who gave them life.

In my Father’s house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also.

“The Family: A Proclamation to the World” was read by President Gordon B. Hinckley at the general Relief Society meeting in September 1995. It was signed by the First Presidency and the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles. It is printed in the Ensign, Nov. 1995, page 102.

\[Heavenly Father’s\] divine plan of happiness enables family relationships to be perpetuated beyond the grave. Sacred ordinances and covenants available in holy temples make it possible for individuals to return to the presence of God and for families to be united eternally.
The trail ends in a welcome.

story.title: Job’s testimony in suffering

blocks.text: Job lost his children, his health, and his wealth. His friends blamed him. In the middle of all of it, he said what he knew.

For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth: And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God: Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another; though my reins be consumed within me.
Job did not know why he suffered. But he knew his Redeemer lived, and that he would see God. That is the heart of the plan. Even on the steepest part of the trail, we can know where it ends.

application.text: First, find your “You are here” spot. Where are you on the trail right now? Write one sentence. Second, choose one next step that moves you toward home. Make it small and doable. Third, tell someone you trust about the trail. We walk better together.

opening.text: Most good stories have three parts. A beginning that sets things up. A middle where things get hard. And an ending that makes sense of it all. If you only see the middle, the story can look like a mess.
Our lives are a three-part story too. God has shown us all three parts in the plan of happiness. I would like to talk about it.

mainMessage.text: The first part happened before we were born, when we lived with God and agreed to His plan. The second part is now, when we are here to learn, choose, and grow. The third part comes after, when we return to God. Jesus Christ is the hero who makes the ending possible. And our families can be part of that ending.

blocks.text: Part one: before.

The story did not start at birth. Abraham saw the spirits who lived before the world was made, and the Lord said he was chosen before he was born. And the sons of God shouted for joy when the earth was laid.

Now the Lord had shown unto me, Abraham, the intelligences that were organized before the world was; and among all these there were many of the noble and great ones; And God saw these souls that they were good, and he stood in the midst of them, and he said: These I will make my rulers; for he stood among those that were spirits, and he saw that they were good; and he said unto me: Abraham, thou art one of them; thou wast chosen before thou wast born.
Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding. . . . When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
President Spencer W. Kimball wrote this in his book Faith Precedes the Miracle, page 97. It is a book, not a conference talk.

If we looked at mortality as the whole of existence, then pain, sorrow, failure, and short life would be calamity. But if we look upon life as an eternal thing stretching far into the premortal past and on into the eternal post-death future, then all happenings may be put in proper perspective.
If you only watch the middle, you miss the point.
The story was written by a loving Father.
God set the stage. An earth would be made. We would be tested there. Those who follow Him would be given more. Alma called the whole thing the great plan of happiness.

The Creation, the Fall, and the Atonement were planned long before the actual work of the Creation began.
The ending was in view before the story began.
The hero steps forward.

Every good story has a hero. In this one, the Beloved Son said, “Father, thy will be done, and the glory be thine forever.” Alma taught that without an atonement, all would perish. He is the reason the story can end well.

The hero gave everything. That is why the ending is safe.
Part two: the middle.
The middle is where the work happens. It is often the hardest part to watch. Adam fell that men might be, and men are that they might have joy. And this life is the time to prepare to meet God.
Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy.

The middle is where we are changed.
We are not characters. We are authors.

In this story, we help write our own chapters. Lehi taught that we are free to choose liberty and eternal life or captivity and death. Joshua said, choose you this day. Our choices shape how our story goes.

story.title: Joseph Smith in Liberty Jail

blocks.text: Joseph Smith was held for months in a cold, crowded jail. He cried out and asked where God was. The Lord answered.

My son, peace be unto thy soul; thine adversity and thine afflictions shall be but a small moment; And then, if thou endure it well, God shall exalt thee on high; thou shalt triumph over all thy foes.
In the middle of the story, the Lord reminded Joseph that the middle is not the end. The hard chapter is “but a small moment.” When we trust the plan, we can wait for the next chapter.

application.text: First, name the “chapter” you are in. Is it a good one, or a hard one? Second, remind yourself that this is the middle, not the end. Write one line of hope. Third, help someone else through their middle chapter this week, with a visit or a call.
